lessons.title: Asking for Directions: Where is...?

When giving directions, use landmarks. Or "å¨å¸åºå¯¹é¢ï¼å³æ" (ZÃ i shÃ¬chÇng duÃ¬miÃ n, yÃ²u guÇi) â "Opposite the market, turn right." Use å¨ (zÃ i) for location: å¨å·¦è¾¹ (zÃ i zuÇbiÄn) = on the left, å¨å³è¾¹ (zÃ i yÃ²ubiÄn) = on the right.

Be clear and slow. If someone doesn't understand, repeat and use hand gestures. In Mandarin, you can say: "å...ç¶å..." (xiÄn... rÃ¡nhÃ²u...) = first... then... Example: "åä¸ç´èµ°ï¼ç¶åå·¦æï¼åå³æ" (XiÄn yÄ«zhÃ­ zÇu, rÃ¡nhÃ²u zuÇ guÇi, zÃ i yÃ²u guÇi) â "First go straight, then turn left, then turn right." For instance, from your house to the nearest bus stop: "åºé¨å³æï¼ä¸ç´èµ°50ç±³ï¼å·¦æï¼åèµ°20ç±³ï¼å°±å°äº" (ChÅ«mÃ©n yÃ²u guÇi, yÄ«zhÃ­ zÇu wÇshÃ­ mÇ, zuÇ guÇi, zÃ i zÇu Ã¨rshÃ­ mÇ, jiÃ¹ dÃ o le) â "Exit and turn right, go straight 50 meters, turn left, then walk 20 meters, and you arrive." lessons.title: Role-Play: Getting to the Train Station
lessons.body:

If you don't understand, say: "è¯·è¯´æ¢ä¸ç¹" (QÇng shuÅ mÃ n yÄ«diÇn) â "Please speak slower." Or "æå¬ä¸æ" (WÇ tÄ«ng bÃ¹ dÇng) â "I don't understand."

Next, you decide to take a taxi. You flag one and say: "è¯·å°ç«è½¦ç«" (QÇng dÃ o huÇchÄzhÃ n) â "Please go to the train station." The driver asks: "åªä¸ªç«è½¦ç«?" During the ride, you might say: "åé¢å³æ" (QiÃ¡nmiÃ n yÃ²u guÇi) â "Turn right ahead." When you arrive: "å¤å°é±?" (DuÅshÇo qiÃ¡n?) â "How much?" You pay and say: "è°¢è°¢" (XiÃ¨xiÃ¨) â "Thank you."

At the station, you need to buy a ticket. Go to the ticket office (å®ç¥¨å¤, shÃ²upiÃ ochÃ¹) and say: "æè¦ä¸å¼ å°...çç¥¨" (WÇ yÃ o yÄ« zhÄng dÃ o... de piÃ o) â "I want one ticket to..." For example, if you're in Nairobi and going to Mombasa: "æè¦ä¸å¼ å°èå·´è¨çç¥¨" (WÇ yÃ o yÄ« zhÄng dÃ o MÃ©ngbÄsÃ  de piÃ o). The clerk asks: "å å¼ ?" (JÇ zhÄng?) â "How many?" You say: "ä¸å¼ " (YÄ« zhÄng). Then ask: "å¤å°é±?" (DuÅshÇo qiÃ¡n?) â "How much?" And "å ç¹åºå?" (JÇ diÇn chÅ«fÄ?) â "What time does it depart?"

After buying the ticket, find the platform (ç«å°, zhÃ ntÃ¡i). Ask: "è¯·é®ï¼ç«å°å¨åªé?" (QÇngwÃ¨n, zhÃ ntÃ¡i zÃ i nÇlÇ?) â "Excuse me, where is the platform?" Look for signs: å¥å£ (rÃ¹kÇu) = entrance, åºå£ (chÅ«kÇu) = exit, åè½¦å®¤ (hÃ²uchÄshÃ¬) = waiting room. If you need help, go to the information desk (é®è¯¢å¤, wÃ¨nxÃºnchÃ¹). Say: "è¯·é®ï¼å»èå·´è¨çç«è½¦å¨åªä¸ªç«å°?" (QÇngwÃ¨n, qÃ¹ MÃ©ngbÄsÃ  de huÇchÄ zÃ i nÇge zhÃ ntÃ¡i?) â "Excuse me, which platform is the train to Mombasa?"

After practicing, you'll be ready to navigate transportation in Mandarin-speaking environments, whether in Africa or abroad.
